'''Takata Shrine''' (高田神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in [[Hida City]], {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|en|Gifu Prefecture|qid=Q131277|lt=Gifu Prefecture}}, formerly part of {{ill|Yoshiki District|en|Yoshiki District|qid=Q8056119|lt=Yoshiki District}} in [[Furukawa Town]].

It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|式内社|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō}} for {{ill|Hida Province|en|Hida Province|qid=Q1056535|lt=Hida Province}}. Another theory suggests that {{ill|Kifune Shrine (Hida City)|ja|貴船神社 (飛騨市)|2=ja|3=貴船神社 (飛騨市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kifune Shrine (Hida)|13=User:Immanuelle/Kifune Shrine (Hida City)}} is the site of the original Takata Shrine.

== History ==
The exact founding date is unknown. One theory states that it was established in the 6th year of Emperor Bidatsu (577 CE) when the [[Nihamabe|Hihamabe]] clan was stationed in Hida Province, and their {{ill|Tomonomiyatsuko|lt=Tomonomiyatsuko|lt=Tomo no Miyatsuko|ja|伴造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomo no Miyatsuko|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} enshrined Takamimusubi no Mikoto.

During the [[Kenmu Restoration]], [[Anekōji Ietsuna]] was a11ointed governor of Hida Province in 1334 and showed great reverence for Takata Shrine. He established a residence adjacent to the shrine, which became the political center of Hida. However, after the fall of the {{ill|Anekōji clan|en|Anekōji clan|qid=Q10943126|lt=Anekōji clan}} to {{ill|Kanamori Nagachika|en|Kanamori Nagachika|qid=Q8190652|lt=Kanamori Nagachika}}, the shrine's prominence declined.

In the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}, the shrine was renamed "Hakusan Shrine" or "Hakusan Gongen Shrine." During the {{ill|Bunka|en|Bunka|qid=Q1373146|lt=Bunka era}} (1804–1818), the {{ill|Urabe clan|ja|吉田家|2=ja|3=卜部氏|lt=Yoshida family|comment=Might be more of a redirect with potential but this is strictly potential right now|lt=Yoshida clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Urabe clan}} identified it as the Takata Shrine listed in the Engishiki, and it was renamed accordingly. The formal designation of Takata Shrine as a Shikinaisha was granted in 1870 (Meiji 3).

In 1907 (Meiji 40), the shrine incorporated Suwa Shrine, Tado Shrine, and Kamo Shrine.

* Main deity
** [[Takamimusubi|Takamimusubi no Mikoto]]
* Enshrined Deities
** [[:en:Kikurihime no Kami|Hakusan-hime no Kami]]
** [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata no Mikoto]]

** [[Amatsuhikone|Amatsuhikone no Mikoto]]

== festival ==
The festival highlights include the Kagura Lion Dance, [[matchlock]] gun firings, and a portable shrine procession.

* Kagura Lion Dance
** A two-person [[shishi-mai]] performed by male and female pairs, featuring six different routines. It is designated as an Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property of {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|en|Gifu Prefecture|qid=Q131277|lt=Gifu Prefecture}}.<ref name="kagurajishi">{{Cite web|language=ja|date= |url=http://www.pref.gifu.lg.jp/kyoiku-bunka-sports/bunka-geijutsu/bunkazai-zuroku/bunkazai-zuroku/mumin/hidasi/takadajinnjya.html |title=Kagura Lion Dance of Takata Shrine |publisher=Gifu Prefecture |accessdate=2013-04-22}}</ref> The dance is performed several times during the festival.
* Matchlock Gun Firings
** Conducted at key points of the festival to purify the sacred grounds. The matchlocks are said to have been donated during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|Sengoku period|qid=Q204023|lt=Sengoku period}} by {{ill|Anekōji Tokimitsu|ja|姉小路時光|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Anekōji Tokimitsu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
* Portable Shrine Procession
** A procession including {{ill|Cleyera japonica|en|Cleyera japonica|qid=Q775470|lt=Cleyera japonica}}, {{ill|Tengu|en|Tengu|qid=Q742360|lt=Tengu}}, armored warriors, chicken fights, male and female lions, drums, flutes, {{ill|Miko|en|Miko|qid=Q1047139|lt=Miko}}, and the mikoshi, comprising several hundred participants.

== Cultural Properties ==
;Important Intangible Folk Cultural Properties of Gifu Prefecture

;Designated Tangible Cultural Properties of Hida City
* Kabuto (helmet) of Takata Shrine<ref name="furukawacho_bunkazai">{{Cite web|language=ja|date= |url=http://www.pamph-navi.jp/art/view_dynamic/pdfView.php?src=pam10008025 |title=Furukawa Town Cultural Property Guide |format=PDF |publisher=Hida City |accessdate=2013-04-22}}</ref>
* Statues of Takata Shrine Guardians<ref name="furukawacho_bunkazai" />
;Designated Natural Monuments of Hida City
* Five Great Cedars of Takata Shrine<ref name="furukawacho_bunkazai" />

** A procession including {{ill|Cleyera japonica|en|Cleyera japonica|qid=Q775470|lt=Cleyera japonica}}, {{ill|Tengu|en|Tengu|qid=Q742360|lt=Tengu}}, armored warriors, chicken fights, male and female lions, drums, flutes, {{ill|Miko|en|Miko|qid=Q1047139|lt=Miko}}, and the mikoshi, comprising several hundred participants.
